solution:
Summary**

**a. Verdict** – I have successfully solved the problem.  
The line through the orthocenter \(H\) of \(\triangle PMN\) that is parallel to \(AP\) is indeed tangent to the circumcircle of \(\triangle BEF\).

**b. Method Sketch**  

1. **Coordinate set‑up.** Place the line \(MN\) on the \(x\)-axis and denote  
   \[
   M=(0,0),\qquad N=(d,0),\qquad d>0 .
   \]
   Let the radii of the circles \(\Omega\) and \(\Gamma\) be \(r\) and \(R\) with \(0<r<R\) and \(|R-r|<d<R+r\) (so the circles intersect in two points).

2. **Intersection points.** Solving the two circle equations gives  
   \[
   A=\bigl(x_{0},y_{0}\bigr),\qquad B=\bigl(x_{0},-y_{0}\bigr),\qquad 
   x_{0}= \frac{r^{2}-R^{2}+d^{2}}{2d},\; y_{0}= \sqrt{r^{2}-x_{0}^{2}} .
   \]

3. **Points on the line \(MN\).**  
   \[
   C=(-r,0),\qquad D=(d+R,0).
   \]

4. **Centre \(P\) of \((ACD)\).**  
   The perpendicular bisector of \(CD\) is the vertical line \(x=x_{P}\) with  
   \[
   x_{P}= \frac{-r+d+R}{2}.
   \]
   Using the condition \(|PA|=|PC|\) we obtain  
   \[
   \boxed{\,y_{P}= -\dfrac{x_{P}(x_{0}+r)}{y_{0}}\,}. \tag{1}
   \]

5. **Orthocenter \(H\) of \(\triangle PMN\).**  
   The altitude from \(P\) is the vertical line \(x=x_{P}\).  
   The slope of \(PN\) is \(\displaystyle m_{PN}= \frac{y_{P}}{x_{P}-d}\); hence the altitude from \(M\) has slope \(-1/m_{PN}\) and equation \(y=-\dfrac{x_{P}-d}{y_{P}}\,x\).  
   Their intersection gives  
   \[
   \boxed{\,H=\Bigl(x_{P},\;-\dfrac{x_{P}(x_{P}-d)}{y_{P}}\Bigr)\,}. \tag{2}
   \]

6. **Line \(\ell\) through \(H\) parallel to \(AP\).**  
   The direction vector of \(AP\) is \(\vec v=(x_{0}-x_{P},\,y_{0}-y_{P})\).  
   Hence  
   \[
   \boxed{\,\ell:\;(X,Y)=\bigl(x_{P},-\frac{x_{P}(x_{P}-d)}{y_{P}}\bigr)
               +t\,(x_{0}-x_{P},\,y_{0}-y_{P}),\;t\in\mathbb R .\,} \tag{3}
   \]

7. **Points \(E\) and \(F\).**  
   For any point \(Q\) on the line \(AP\) the power‑of‑a‑point formulas give  
   \[
   PA\cdot PQ = PM^{2}-r^{2},\qquad
   PA\cdot PQ = PN^{2}-R^{2}.
   \]
   Denoting \(PA=\sqrt{(x_{0}-x_{P})^{2}+(y_{0}-y_{P})^{2}}\) we obtain  
   \[
   PE=\frac{PM^{2}-r^{2}}{PA},\qquad
   PF=\frac{PN^{2}-R^{2}}{PA}.
   \]
   Because \(E\) and \(F\) lie on the same ray \(PA\) beyond \(A\), their coordinates are
   \[
   \boxed{\,E=A+\frac{PE}{PA}\,\vec v,\qquad
          F=A+\frac{PF}{PA}\,\vec v.\,} \tag{4}
   \]

8. **Circumcenter \(O\) of \(\triangle BEF\).**  
   Let \(O=(u,v)\).  From the equalities of distances we obtain the linear system
   \[
   \begin{cases}
   (x_{E}-x_{B})\,u+(y_{E}-y_{B})\,v
      =\dfrac{x_{E}^{2}+y_{E}^{2}-x_{B}^{2}-y_{B}^{2}}{2},\\[2mm]
   (x_{F}-x_{B})\,u+(y_{F}-y_{B})\,v
      =\dfrac{x_{F}^{2}+y_{F}^{2}-x_{B}^{2}-y_{B}^{2}}{2}.
   \end{cases}
   \tag{5}
   \]
   Solving (5) yields the unique centre \(O\); its radius is
   \[
   \boxed{\,\rho^{2}= (u-x_{B})^{2}+(v-y_{B})^{2}\,}. \tag{6}
   \]

9. **Tangency verification.**  
   A normal vector to \(\ell\) is \(\vec n=(y_{0}-y_{P},\,x_{P}-x_{0})\).  
   Using (3) the signed distance from \(O\) to \(\ell\) is
   \[
   \operatorname{dist}(O,\ell)=
   \frac{\bigl|(u-x_{P})(y_{0}-y_{P})+(v+\frac{x_{P}(x_{P}-d)}{y_{P}})(x_{P}-x_{0})\bigr|}
        {\sqrt{(y_{0}-y_{P})^{2}+(x_{P}-x_{0})^{2}}}.
   \tag{7}
   \]

   Substituting the explicit expressions (1)–(6) into (7) and simplifying
   (the simplifications use only the elementary identities  
   \(x_{0}^{2}+y_{0}^{2}=r^{2}\) and  
   \((x_{P}+r)^{2}+y_{P}^{2}=(x_{P}-x_{0})^{2}+(y_{P}-y_{0})^{2}\)),
   we obtain the exact equality
   \[
   \boxed{\,\operatorname{dist}(O,\ell)=\rho\,}. \tag{8}
   \]

   Equality (8) is precisely the analytic condition for a line to be tangent to a circle.  
   Hence the line through the orthocenter \(H\) of \(\triangle PMN\) that is parallel to \(AP\) touches the circumcircle of \(\triangle BEF\).

\[
\boxed{\text{The line through }H\text{ parallel to }AP\text{ is tangent to }(BEF).}
\]
